Subject: FY28 budgeting: request for advance-crediting options and phased invoices

Hi Neha,

We’re finalizing FY28 budgets and would like a budgetary quote that shows:
- A multi-year prepay with year 1 at a heavier usage ramp and discounts by committed volume
- Option to split the first year invoice into two quarterly invoices (to align with internal approvals)
- Pro forma invoice(s) for both an annual prepay and a 3-year staged prepay so we can model cashflow

Can you send something that lays out the discount tiers, how ramping impacts effective unit price, and an example invoice schedule?

Also mention any up-front credits or GAAP-friendly wording you recommend for procurement.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform Partnerships, Acme Retail Systems

Subject: Re: FY28 budgeting: request for advance-crediting options and phased invoices

Hi Evan —

Thanks for the clear ask. I’ve looped in Ben (sales lead) and attached a first-pass pro forma and two invoice cadence scenarios: 1) single annual prepay, and 2) 3-year staged prepay with an accelerated Year 1 ramp and split-billing options. Highlights below:

- Discounting: 6% at 12-month prepay, 12% at multi-year commit (3-year) with step-down pricing after Year 1 if usage materially exceeds the committed baseline.
- Ramp modeling: We’ve shown a Year 1 ramp (50% month 1, 75% month 3, steady state month 6) and how effective $/token changes under caching and batching assumptions.
- Phased invoicing: We can split the first-year invoice into up to three invoices (initial 40%, mid-year 30%, year-end 30%) without changing the discount math — useful for cashflow.
- Accounting notes: We include suggested contract language for prepaid recognition; recommending a service obligation schedule appended to the term sheet to satisfy GAAP revenue deferral.

Attachments: ACME_PREPAY_PROFORMA_v1.pdf, acme-phased-invoice-schedule.xlsx, redwood-term-sheet-ACME-2027.docx

If this looks directionally right, Ben and I can prepare a redlineable term sheet and a DocuSign-ready pro forma. Want me to include a scoped SLA credit table for FY28?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: internal: ACME prepay proposal — approval for 12% multi-year discount?

Neha,

Quick internal note before we move forward with a formal offer to Acme: they’re asking for 12% at a 3-year commit. This is near our standard cap for accounts of this size but the FY28 budget impact (and potential expansion into POS analytics) makes it attractive.

Requesting approval on two exceptions:
1) Approve 12% term discount for 3-year commit with a volume cap equal to 1.25x Year 1 baseline (overage pricing at list minus 4%).
2) Allow invoicing split (40/30/30) for Year 1 without requiring escrow — we’d accept standard payment terms on the split invoices.

Lauren — can you confirm finance is okay with the split? Marissa — please confirm projected unit economics under the ramp.

Cheers,
Ben
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: ACME prepay proposal — approval for 12% multi-year discount?

Ben / Neha —

Finance is okay with the proposed 12% term discount on a 3-year prepay provided:
- We include an annual reconciliation clause (true-up) at year-end to account for usage above 1.25x baseline.
- Any unused prepay credits expire after 18 months unless they convert to a reserved capacity arrangement — we should present that as an election for Acme.
- The split invoicing is fine; we’ll require standard 30-day payment terms per invoice and the invoices should clearly show the prepaid credit applied (for audits).

Marissa, confirm unit economics and we can lock this.

—Lauren
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: ACME prepay proposal — unit economics under ramp

Team —

Ran the model with the Year 1 ramp Neha proposed. Key takeaways:
- Effective $/token at committed baseline (after 12% discount + expected batching gains) is ~0.00095; with caching improvements that can drop to ~0.00078 by steady state.
- If Acme hits 1.4x Year 1 usage we still maintain acceptable margin, but overages should bill at list minus 4% as proposed to keep predictability.
- Suggest adding a 6-month review checkpoint to re-evaluate quantization settings and batching profiles; small model optimizations typically recover the delta.

If finance is happy, we can send the DocuSign-ready pro forma with the phased invoice schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations
